claims.text: An ML-driven framework can rapidly identify candidate RHEA compositions.
ML-designed RHEAs will combine higher strength, improved ductility, and lower density.
ML-designed candidates will outperform alloys discovered through conventional trial-and-error methods.
Conventional RHEA compositions are selected from limited trial-and-error approaches, including thermo-kinetic analysis and incremental microstructure tuning.
Curated experimental and simulation datasets can be used to train an ML model for RHEA design.
The ML model can predict mechanical properties and density from composition and processing parameters.
Phase distribution, grain size, and lattice distortion mediate the trade-off among RHEA strength, ductility, and density.
An ML framework can identify compositional regimes that optimally combine refractory and lighter elements.
These compositional regimes produce optimal lattice distortion and phase stability.
Optimal lattice distortion and phase stability enhance resistance to dislocation motion and thereby improve strength.
The identified compositional regimes promote ductile deformation mechanisms and thereby improve ductility.
Incorporating lighter elements reduces overall alloy density.
The proposed method applies to multi-principal-element RHEAs containing typically five or more refractory elements.
The method is applicable only within the compositional domain represented in the training dataset, while extrapolation may require model updating.
Incomplete or imbalanced training data and complex multicomponent interactions may reduce prediction accuracy.
